hypothesis: Whole-paper extraction makes competing endpoint families crowd each other out; one call per family should recover more.
basis: Three prior measurements pointed this way: 39 vs 168 candidate slots, 1 vs 7 candidates per repair task, v4 per-experiment 12/15 vs whole-paper compact 10/15.
design: GP-006, structure-aware packet, candidate slots on. Five endpoint families, one codex turn each.
verdict: Does not pay. Splitting by endpoint family costs 5 turns instead of 1 and recovers nothing extra.
why_it_probably_failed: GO-004 belongs to cell_target_effect, and that scope returned zero outcomes even with the family to itself and its six slots in hand. Turn size was not what was blocking it, so the smaller-unit principle does not extend from candidate slots and repair tasks to extraction scope.
note: A real defect was found and fixed on the way: omitting required_candidate_ids parsed slot-bearing replies against the contract that forbids candidate_dispositions, rejecting all five scopes before this measurement was possible.
